newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares soar to record high.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares soar to record high.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares soared to record highs on Friday on the back of active buying by foreign and local investors hopeful of a normal rainy season.

The key 57-share industrial index leapt 139.84 points -- or 1.8 percent -- to break through the psychological 8,000 barrier, ending at an all time peak of 8,045.75. This was a surge of 429.33 points on the week.
"The early rain showers being experienced seem to have strengthened investor sentiment," one broker said.
The rains are essential for the country's agriculture-powered economy.

Another analyst said foreign investors were also showing keen interest in local shares as the Zimbabwe dollar stabilised against major foreign currencies after losing a lot of ground against them at the end of September and early October.
"Most people believe that the (Zimbabwe) dollar won't go much lower than it has gone now so foreigners are back in the market," he said.

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Friday, newly-listed hotel and supermarkets group Meikles Africa led the day's winners, leaping 700 cents to 3,000. Tobacco firm BAT jumped 200 cents to 1,700 while winery Cairns rose 50 cents to 1,000 and clothing retailer Truworths gained 30 cents to 780.
Rubber and agricultural products manufacturer Acacia, transport group Clan and pork processor Colcom all added 10 cents to 260, 260 and 350 respectively.
Bankers Barclays and FMB, blue-chip conglomerate Delta, engineering firm Mash and hotel chain Zimsun all traded at previous levels in reasonable turnover of shares.
A couple of stocks bucked the trend. Appliances-maker Capri and tyre manufacturer Dunlop each shed 10 cents to 105 and 180 respectively.
Minings remained quiet on a lacklustre gold bullion price and Falgold lost 10 cents to 130.
Wankie Colliery added 10 cents to 360, but it was inadequate to shore up the seven-share index which slipped a marginal 0.39 points to 1,230.25. It lost 18.52 points on the week.
